# 1 Maccabees Chapter 14 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the one hundred and seventy-second year King Demetrius assembled his forces and went into Media to get auxiliary troops to fight against Trypho.

**2** And Arsaces the king of Persia and Media heard that Demetrius had entered his territories, and he sent one of his generals to take him alive.

**3** And he went out and struck the army of Demetrius and seized him and brought him to Arsaces, who put him under guard.

**4** And the land of Judah was at rest all the days of Simon, and he sought the good of his nation, and his rule and his glory pleased them well all his days.

**5** And among his glorious deeds was this: he took Joppa as a harbor and made a way to the islands of the sea.

**6** And he enlarged the borders of his nation and gained possession of the land.

**7** And he gathered many captives and had dominion over Gazara and Beth-zur and the citadel, and he removed its uncleannesses from it; and there was none who resisted him.

**8** And they tilled their land in peace, and the land gave its produce and the trees of the plain their fruit.

**9** Old men sat in the streets and talked together about good things, and the young men put on glorious and warlike apparel.

**10** He provided food for the cities and furnished them with the means of defense, until his glorious name was known to the end of the earth.

**11** He made peace in the land and Israel rejoiced with great joy.

**12** And each man sat under his vine and under his fig tree, and there was none to make them afraid.

**13** And no one was left in the land to fight against them, and the kings were crushed in those days.

**14** And he strengthened all the poor of his people; he sought out the law and removed every lawless and wicked man.

**15** He made the sanctuary glorious and multiplied the sacred vessels.

**16** And the news was heard in Rome and as far as Sparta that Jonathan had died, and they were deeply grieved.

**17** But when they heard that Simon his brother had become high priest in his place and that he ruled over the country and the cities in it,

**18** they wrote to him on bronze tablets to renew with him the friendship and alliance they had established with Judas and Jonathan his brothers.

**19** And they were read before the assembly in Jerusalem.

**20** And this is the copy of the letters that the Spartans sent: "The rulers and the city of the Spartans to Simon the great priest and to the elders and the priests and the rest of the Jewish people, brothers, greetings.

**21** The envoys who were sent to our people reported to us about your glory and honor, and we were glad at their coming.

**22** And what they said we wrote down in the decrees of the people: Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, envoys of the Jews, came to us to renew the friendship with us.

**23** And it pleased the people to receive the men with honor and to put a copy of their words in the public archives, that the people of the Spartans might have a record of it. And a copy of this was sent to Simon the great priest."

**24** After this Simon sent Numenius to Rome with a great gold shield weighing a thousand minas to confirm the alliance with them.

**25** And when the people heard these things, they said: "What thanks shall we give to Simon and his sons?

**26** For he and his brothers and his father's house have stood firm and fought off the enemies of Israel and have established his freedom." And they wrote on bronze tablets and set them up on pillars on Mount Zion.

**27** And this is the copy of the writing: "On the eighteenth day of Elul in the one hundred and seventy-second year — and this is the third year of Simon the great high priest —

**28** in Asaramel, in a great assembly of priests and of the people and of the rulers of the nation and of the elders of the country, it was proclaimed:

**29** Since wars have often occurred in our land, Simon son of Mattathias of the family of Joarib and his brothers have put themselves in danger and resisted the enemies of their nation, in order that their sanctuary might be maintained and the law be upheld; and they glorified their nation with great glory.

**30** Jonathan rallied his nation and became their high priest, and was gathered to his people.

**31** And their enemies sought to invade their land and lay hands on their sanctuary.

**32** Then Simon rose up and fought for his nation and spent much of his own money; he armed the men of valor of his nation and gave them wages.

**33** He fortified the cities of Judea and Beth-zur on the borders of Judea, where formerly the weapons of the enemies had been, and he put a garrison of Jewish men there.

**34** He also fortified Joppa which is by the sea and Gazara which is on the borders of Azotus, where the enemies had formerly dwelt, and he settled Jews there and provided whatever was needed for the restoration of these cities.

**35** And the people saw Simon's faithfulness and the glory which he sought to bring on his nation, and they made him their leader and high priest because of all these things, and because of the righteousness and faithfulness which he had maintained toward his nation, and because he sought in every way to exalt his people.

**36** And in his days things prospered in his hands, so that the Gentiles were removed from their land and also those who were in the city of David in Jerusalem who had built themselves a citadel from which they used to go out and defile all the surroundings of the sanctuary and inflict great harm on its purity.

**37** And he settled Jewish men in it and fortified it for the security of the land and of the city, and he raised the height of the walls of Jerusalem.

**38** And King Demetrius confirmed him in the high priesthood because of these things,

**39** and he made him one of his friends and honored him with great honor.

**40** For he had heard that the Romans had called the Jews friends and allies and brothers and that they had received the envoys of Simon with honor.

**41** And the Jews and their priests were pleased that Simon should be their leader and high priest forever, until there should arise a faithful prophet;

**42** and that he should be over them as general and that he should take charge of the sanctuary and that he should appoint officers over their tasks and over the country and over the weapons and over the strongholds;

**43** and that he should take charge of the sanctuary, and that all contracts in the country should be written in his name, and that he should put on purple and wear gold;

**44** and that it should not be lawful for any of the people or of the priests to annul any of these things or to contradict what he says, or to convene an assembly in the country without him, or to be clothed in purple or to wear a gold buckle.

**45** And whoever acted contrary to these things or annulled any of these things should be liable to punishment.

**46** And all the people approved of ordaining these things for Simon, and Simon accepted and was pleased to be high priest and to be general and ethnarch of the Jews and of the priests, and to be the protector of them all.

**47** And they commanded to put this writing on bronze tablets and to set it up in the precinct of the sanctuary in a conspicuous place;

**48** and to put copies of it in the treasury so that Simon and his sons might have them.
